newsitem.title: USA: American Air pilots say unlikely to vote today.
newsitem.headline: American Air pilots say unlikely to vote today.

text.p: The board of the American Airlines pilots union said on Thursday it is unlikely that its directors will get to a vote on the carrier's latest labor contract proposal.
"It looks like there is only a remote possibility of a vote today," said Wally Pitts, spokesman for the Allied Pilots Association. APA represents about 9,300 American Airlines pilots.
Pitts said the issue of who will fly smaller jets at American Airlines' regional carrier, American Eagle, remained at the centre of the meeting this afternoon.
American Airlines pilots are concerned they may lose routes to American Eagle if American Airlines buys new smaller jets for the regional subsidiary.
"The members today are trying to educate themselves on the small jet issue and that takes time," Pitts told a news conference in suburban Chicago where the meetings are being held.
"When the board meets, they leave no stone unturned. That's what going on today," Pitts said. The board has been meeting since 0900 CST (1000 EST) and has taken only three short breaks.
Pitts said that it looks like the vote by the board could be close whenever it takes place. "It could be a close vote, but you never really know until the hands are in the air," he said.
